messages.subject: New version of the JGR R Console released
messages.subject_clean: New version of the JGR R Console released
messages.body_plain:
JGR Version 1.7-4 has been released to CRAN and is propagating across the mirrors.

JGR Description:
Java GUI for R - cross-platform, universal and unified Graphical User Interface for R. For full functionality on Windows and Mac OS X JGR requires a start application which depends on your OS. This can be downloaded from JGR's website: http://rforge.net/JGR/

Changes and Features:
1. In editor, run on an empty selection runs line and advances caret.

2. The editor now has an option to format ugly / poorly written R code. Simply select the ugly code you wish to beautify then hit the "Format Selection" menu option, and the code will be reformatted using good style guidelines (See also the formatR package).

3. A preference item controlling italicized comments has been added.

4. The data loader uses the to.data.frame=TRUE in the read.spss function for .sav files

messages.subject: New Version of Deducer released
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Version 0.4-3 of Deducer is released and making its way to all the
CRAN mirrors. There has been a lot of refactoring of the Data Viewer
code, so please let me know if you encounter any bugs.

Changes:
1. Fixed bugs in some of the advanced options in the plot builder
   (thanks to Erich Studerus for the bug reports)
2. Data viewer size restricted to screen size
3. Added k-sample post-hoc comparisons
4. Factored back end to make it easier to plug deducer into different consoles
5. Refactored the Data viewer to be plug-in friendly
6. Added sort to data view column contextual menus
7. Added Links to manual/videos in the default data viewer panel

Best,
Ian

messages.subject: Re: deducer date time data
messages.body_plain:
Bruce,

Deducer 0.4-3 added support for dates and times to the data viewer, so make sure you have the latest version of the package. When converting from strings, the viewer assumes that the format is year/month/day rather than the day/month/year of your data. So you will have to use the command line to get your variables into the right class.

There is a limitation on the size of data that the data viewer can handle. I hope to remove this limitation in a future release. Experimenting with my own system, the data viewer starts to choke up after 25 million cells ( I tried a set with 500,000 observations and 50 variables). If you work with large datasets, I recommend just keeping the data viewer closed.

Ian

messages.subject: Re: deducer date time data
messages.body_plain:
Bruce,

So I've added better date and time conversion to the data viewer,
supporting a variety of formats. There is really no reason the user
should be limited to the 2010-10-10 format. This will be available in
the 0.4-4 release of deducer.

To do what you want, you do need to write a few lines of R code to
manipulate the Time variable into a numeric format. Perhaps I'll add a
string manipulation dialog at some point, but I don't see that
happening too soon.

ian

Mormoopids <- read.table("/Users/ianfellows/Downloads/Mormoopids.CSV",header=T,sep=",",quote="")
#open data dialog
Mormoopids[,3]<-as.Date(Mormoopids[,3], format= '%m/%d/%Y')
#Deducer 0.4-4 Data viewer type conversion

#hand written code to convert time into numeric
tmp <- strsplit(Mormoopids$Time,":")
Mormoopids$Hour <- sapply(tmp,function(x) as.numeric(x[1]) +
as.numeric(x[2])/60 )
#end hand written code

#plot builder
dev.new <http://dev.new>()
ggplot() +
	geom_density(aes(x = Hour,colour = Species),data=Mormoopids) +
	theme_bw()

messages.subject: Consistent Error with t tests
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ian

First of all i *love* your program. Honestly prefer it to SPSS and
also much nicer than Rcmdr. Well done.

Using Analysis>Two Sample Test for a data set I am unable to get a
t.test or wilcox.test. Here's some example output (R version 2.11.1);

> print(two.sample.test(formula=d(bDWG) ~ bConcord,
+ data=d.sub,
+ test=t.test,
+ alternative="two.sided")
+ )
Error in tests[[2]] : subscript out of bounds
In addition: Warning message:
In two.sample.test(formula = d(bDWG) ~ bConcord, data = d.sub, test =
t.test,  :
  bDWG must have at least 3 observations per group. Dropping...

I promise that there are *way* more than 3 observations per group ;-)

If i just work 'old skool' and type at the terminal:

> t.test(bDWG ~ bConcord, data=d)

	Welch Two Sample t-test

data:  bDWG by bConcord
t = 6.185, df = 15.798, p-value = 1.385e-05
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
  7.87152 16.09429
sample estimates:
mean in group 0 mean in group 2
      20.538462        8.555556

This is an error that i get consistently. I saw that two.sample.test
is a function in the Deducer library so I hope you'll be able to help
me get out of this problem.

Many thanks
Dr Ben Fox

messages.subject: Re: Custom deducer installation
messages.body_plain:
Misha,

Try the following and let me know if it works.
1. open R and run the code below.
2. copy the output into a bat file (i.e. jgrLaunch.bat)
3. double click on the pat file

jgrLaunchScript <- function(launcher_loc = NULL) {
	win <- Sys.info()[1] == "Windows"
	rhome <- R.home()
	libs <- paste(.libPaths(), sep = ";", collapse = ifelse(win,
		";", ":"))
	if (win) {
		libs <- gsub("/", "\\\\", libs)
		rhome <- gsub("/", "\\\\", rhome)
	}

	if (is.null(launcher_loc)) {
		cat("please select the location of your jgr launcher\n")
		launcher_loc <- file.choose()
	}

	cmd <- paste("set R_HOME=", rhome, "\n", "set R_LIBS=", libs,
		"\n", sep = "")
	if (win) {
		cmd <- paste("set R_HOME=", rhome, "\n", "set R_LIBS=",
			libs, "\n", sep = "")
		cmd <- paste(cmd, launcher_loc, " --rhome=", rhome, " --libpath=",
			libs, sep = "")
	}
	else {
		cmd <- paste("csh\nsetenv R_HOME \"", rhome, "\"\n",
			"setenv R_LIBS \"", libs, "\"\n", sep = "")
		cmd <- paste(cmd, launcher_loc,"/Contents/MacOS/JGR", sep = "")
	}
	if(win)
		cat("\n\nCopy the following into WordPad and save as \"jgrLaunch.bat\"\n\n")
	cat(cmd,"\n")
	cat("\n\n\n")
	invisible(cmd)
}
jgrLaunchScript()

messages.subject: Re: Custom deducer installation
messages.body_plain:
Misha,

I'm glad you finally got it working. I don't know how you had JGR
installed, but not rJava. 99% of the time JGR can be run by just
double clicking on the jgr-1_62.exe launcher. 1% of the time, however,
the user's R set-up is imposible to know a priori, and they must
specify the paths themselves. I view this unacceptably complex.

The development version of JGR now has a new feature to mitigate this
problem. If you can run require(JGR) in R, you should be able to
launch JGR. The steps are as follows

1. Open R

2. Install development JGR by running
install.packages('JGR',,'http://www.rforge.net/')

3. run
library(JGR)
JGR()

note: If you are not running Windows R>=2.12.0 you will need to use
install.packages('JGR',,'http://www.rforge.net/', type="source") to
get the development version of JGR.

Given the vast array of possible set-ups, I'd appreciate it if anyone
with a custom set-up (i.e. double clicking on the launcher doesn't cut
it) could try this and let me know if there are any problems.

Best,
Ian
